sl-kilima-pay-series-a.title: Kilima Pay raises $18m Series A to expand merchant payments into Tanzania
sl-kilima-pay-series-a.summary: Fictional Kenyan payments start-up Kilima Pay closes an $18m Series A to enter Tanzania.

brief.summary:
Kilima Pay, a (fictional) Nairobi-based merchant payments company, has closed an $18m Series A led by Mosi Ventures, with two development finance investors joining.

The company will use the money to launch in Tanzania early next year and to build a working-capital product for its 40,000 merchants.
brief.why: Shows investors still backing payments businesses that can attach lending to transaction data.

sl-zuri-solar-debt.title: Zuri Solar secures $25m local-currency debt for rooftop solar in Nigeria
sl-zuri-solar-debt.summary: Fictional C&I solar developer Zuri Solar raises naira-denominated debt from a local bank consortium.

brief.summary:
Zuri Solar has signed a $25m-equivalent naira debt facility with three Nigerian banks, backed by a partial guarantee from a development finance institution.

The facility funds about 60MW of rooftop systems for factories and shopping centres, priced in naira to remove currency risk for clients.
brief.why: Local-currency debt with a guarantee is becoming the template for distributed energy after naira volatility.

sl-cbk-sandbox.title: Central bank widens regulatory sandbox to cover tokenised deposits
sl-cbk-sandbox.summary: A central bank opens its sandbox to banks testing tokenised deposits for cross-border settlement.

brief.summary:
The central bank said banks can now apply to test tokenised deposits in its sandbox, with cross-border trade settlement as the first use case.

Applications close at the end of next quarter and pilots will be limited in value.
numbers: First cohort of up to 6 banks
brief.why: Gives banks a regulated route into on-chain settlement before stablecoin rules are final.

bt-nyota-agri-seed.title: Nyota Agri raises $3.2m seed to digitise smallholder input credit
bt-nyota-agri-seed.summary: Fictional Ghanaian agritech Nyota Agri closes a $3.2m seed round.

brief.summary:
Nyota Agri, which lends seeds and fertiliser to smallholder farmers against future harvests, has raised a $3.2m seed round.

It says repayment rates are above 95% across 22,000 farmers and plans to add Côte d'Ivoire next season.
brief.why: Input credit tied to offtake is one of the few agri models showing repeatable unit economics.

bt-mosi-logistics.title: Mosi Logistics buys Egyptian last-mile rival in all-share deal
bt-mosi-logistics.summary: Fictional logistics firm Mosi buys a Cairo last-mile operator in an all-share deal.

brief.summary:
Mosi Logistics has agreed to buy a Cairo-based last-mile delivery company, paying entirely in shares.

The combined business will cover five North and East African cities and expects to break even within 18 months.
brief.why: Consolidation is replacing new funding as the exit route for sub-scale African logistics start-ups.

bt-data-centre-lagos.title: Operator breaks ground on 20MW data centre outside Lagos
bt-data-centre-lagos.summary: A data centre operator starts building a 20MW facility, citing AI demand.

brief.summary:
A pan-African data centre operator has started construction on a 20MW campus near Lagos, the first phase of a planned 60MW site.

It is financed with a mix of equity and a project loan, and the first halls are due to open in 2028.
brief.why: Data centres are attracting infrastructure capital that used to go mostly to power and telecoms towers.

kc-fund-close.title: Acacia Growth Partners holds $210m final close for second Africa fund
kc-fund-close.summary: Fictional mid-market PE firm Acacia Growth Partners closes Fund II at $210m.

brief.summary:
Acacia Growth Partners has closed its second fund at $210m, above its $175m target, with roughly half the capital from African pension funds and insurers.

The fund will write $10m to $30m cheques into healthcare, consumer and business services.
brief.why: A rising share of local institutional money is the main change in African fundraising this year.

kc-private-credit.title: Private credit fund lends $40m to West African school group
kc-private-credit.summary: A private credit fund provides $40m of senior debt to a fictional private school group.

brief.summary:
A pan-African private credit fund has provided $40m of senior secured debt to a private school group with campuses in Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal.

The money refinances bank loans and funds four new campuses.
brief.why: Shows private credit moving into education, a sector banks have often avoided.

kc-exit-ipo.title: Consumer goods maker files for listing on regional exchange
kc-exit-ipo.summary: A PE-backed consumer goods company files for an IPO, giving its sponsor a partial exit.

brief.summary:
A PE-backed household goods manufacturer has filed to list on a regional stock exchange, with the sponsor selling part of its stake.

Pricing is expected next month.
brief.why: Public-market exits remain rare; a successful listing would be a useful signal for other sponsors.

demo0001.subject: Rand rallies on rate hopes
demo0001.htmlBody:
The rand

The currency gained about one percent against the dollar as traders priced in a rate cut next quarter. Bond yields fell across the curve, and foreign buyers returned to local government debt for a second week.

Retail results

A large grocery chain reported higher half-year sales, helped by its private-label range, but margins narrowed because of promotions and higher electricity costs. Management kept its dividend unchanged.

Ports

Waiting times at the main container terminal fell for a third straight week after new cranes came into service. Shipping lines said they would review congestion surcharges if the improvement holds.

Unsubscribe · Preferences

demo0002.subject: Dealmaker's log: five fund closes and a solar refinancing
demo0002.htmlBody:
Fund closes

Five funds announced closes this week. The largest was a $210m mid-market buyout fund that beat its target, with about half of the money coming from African pension funds and insurers.

Credit

A rooftop solar developer signed a naira-denominated facility with three local banks, backed by a partial guarantee. Pricing in local currency removes currency risk for its factory and mall customers.

Venture

Payments and agritech led early-stage rounds. A Nairobi payments company raised an $18m Series A, and a Ghanaian input-credit lender closed a $3.2m seed round.

demo0003.subject: Budget season and the eurobond question
demo0003.htmlBody:
Budgets

Two finance ministers tabled budgets that aim to narrow deficits through spending restraint and better tax collection. Both rely on higher commodity revenues that could prove optimistic.

Debt

Officials signalled a possible return to international bond markets next year if spreads keep narrowing. Local banks remain the main buyers of government paper in the meantime.

Commodities

Cocoa prices stayed well above last year's levels, supporting export earnings, although smuggling across borders continues to reduce official volumes.

demo0004.subject: Insurers turn to infrastructure
demo0004.htmlBody:
Insurers

Several large insurers said they would raise their allocations to unlisted infrastructure, citing long-dated cash flows that match their liabilities. Renewable energy and toll roads are the first targets.

Telecoms

A proposed merger between two mobile operators is waiting on competition approval. The regulator has asked for more detail on spectrum holdings and tower-sharing arrangements before it decides.

demo0005.subject: Essay: why local LPs are changing African fundraising
demo0005.htmlBody:
The shift

African pension funds and insurers are committing more money to local private funds, helped by rule changes that let them hold more unlisted assets. In several recent closes they provided close to half of all commitments.

Why it matters

Local capital reduces fund managers' reliance on development finance institutions and changes the terms they negotiate. It also brings demand for currency-hedged share classes and more frequent reporting.
